body.estimand_functional: \(R_{XY}(p)=\Pr_p\{P_x(y)\text{ is identifiable in }G_Z\}=\sum_{S:\operatorname{Fail}(S)=0}\prod_{e\in S}p_e\prod_{e\notin S}(1-p_e),\quad p\in[0,1]^{E^{?}}\)

sampling_model.design: Independent Bernoulli realization of uncertain directed and bidirected edges in a fixed topologically ordered ADMG envelope.
sampling_model.units: The finite vertices \(V\) are fixed; there is no sampling of observational units in the theorem.
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention set \(X\) and outcome set \(Y\) are fixed before the edge realization.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; the real probabilities \(p_e\in[0,1]\) encode structural uncertainty rather than treatment assignment.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; \(p\in[0,1]^{E^{?}}\) and the envelope are computational inputs. Rational coordinates are required only when the exact bit-complexity guarantee is invoked, and no calibration claim for estimated edge probabilities is made.
sampling_model.randomness: Only \(Z\) is random, with mutually independent coordinates.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The edge ID problem is NP-complete.
Lemma 7 states that Algorithm 2 returns an optimal solution to the minimum-cost intervention problem in Equation (2).
We can enumerate all minimal directed Steiner trees in \(O(nm)\) delay and \(O(n+m)\) space.
The minimal transversals can be enumerated in fixed-parameter-linear delay following an FPT preprocessing phase.
Our algorithm runs in time \(O(4^k k\ell N)\).
Source--sink reliability is \(\#\mathrm{P}\)-complete even for acyclic directed planar graphs having vertex degree at most three.
The ID algorithm is complete for identification of interventional distributions in semi-Markovian causal models.
Proposition 1 states that the ID algorithm fails exactly when a hedge exists for the original identification query.
The directed path-conjunction special case admits polynomial-delay enumeration.
Project--join trees support exact weighted model counting by dynamic programming.
Network reliability is fixed-parameter tractable for bounded-treewidth networks.
Counting vertex covers in bipartite graphs is \(\#\mathrm{P}\)-complete.

body.tldr: A probabilistic ADMG currently yields one high-plausibility identifiable realization, not the total chance that a fixed causal query is identifiable or the minimal edge combinations that destroy it.  The project makes those combinations the hyperedges of \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) and compresses every hedge into a \(2b-2\)-edge core plus directed ancestry obligations.  For general \(b\), the proved exact compiler projects deterministic reachability, enumerates raw minimal directed-Steiner witnesses, tests global minimality across every core, and suppresses duplicates canonically; its \(2^{O(b\log(b+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n)(1+W)\) total-time guarantee is explicitly sensitive to the number \(W\) of raw witnesses and is not an accepted-output delay bound.  The enumeration headline is the complete \(b\le2\) labelled transition-DAG and induced-path algorithm with polynomial preprocessing, worst-case delay, exhaustion, and space.  Once \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) is explicit, standard exact literal-weighted CNF model counting on a supplied incidence decomposition yields reliability and all edge sensitivities, while exact successful-realization counting is \(\#\mathrm P\)-complete already at \(b=2\).

project_justification.gap: Ordinary ID certifies failure in one ADMG by a hedge, and edgeID chooses one plausible identifiable subgraph, but neither theory compiles all globally minimal uncertain-edge causes of failure.  The additional general-\(b\) output-delay question remains open because raw candidates from one sparse core can be dominated by an obstruction from another core.
project_justification.niche: Maximum envelope district size \(b\) bounds the local bidirected and forest part of every hedge without bounding its directed ancestry paths or the incidence treewidth of the resulting obstruction hypergraph.  This separates an unconditional candidate-sensitive exact compiler from the stronger partial-extension oracle needed for accepted-output delay.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the sparse-core representation, an unconditional exact general-\(b\) compiler with fixed-parameter polynomial work per raw projected Steiner witness and canonical global filtering, a complete polynomial-delay construction for every \(b\le2\) envelope, the reliability and sensitivity implementation corollaries, and a width-two causal counting-hardness boundary.  It retains general-\(b\) worst-case delay as an explicit open frontier.

body.related_work: Shpitser and Pearl (2008) establish soundness and completeness of ordinary ID through hedge certificates; Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1, \(\mathrm{arXiv}:2307.03750\)) gives the corrected equivalence between ID failure and a hedge for the original query.  These results supply the causal equivalence used here, not support enumeration.  Akbari et al. (2023) formulate probabilistic ADMGs and prove edge ID is NP-complete, while Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025, Definition 6, Algorithm 2, and Lemma 7) use only the vertex-minimal hedges needed for a minimum hitting-set intervention problem in one fixed graph.  Neither work enumerates uncertain-edge-minimal failure supports across all realizations.  Kobayashi, Kurita, and Wasa (2022, Theorem 16) prove linear-delay, polynomial-space enumeration of minimal directed Steiner subgraphs.  Here that theorem is used only for raw witnesses after an injectively labelled deterministic-reachability projection; the local proof supplies support canonicalization, all-core deletion tests, and least-core ownership.  Those filters give candidate-sensitive total time, not general-\(b\) accepted-output delay.  Kenig and Mizrahi (2025) give fixed-parameter delay for minimal transversals when an explicit bounded-incidence-treewidth decomposition is supplied, but bounded causal district size does not bound the incidence treewidth of \(\mathcal O_{XY}\).  Generic explicit-hypergraph dualization likewise does not provide the missing implicit extension oracle coupled to existential core choice and multiple-root reachability, so no quasi-polynomial or fixed-parameter delay conclusion is imported from it.  Samer and Szeider (2010) and Dudek, Phan, and Vardi (2020) provide the standard exact weighted-CNF machinery used after compilation; Goharshady and Mohammadi (2020) place that computation within established reliability methodology.  Provan (1986) and Provan and Ball (1983) supply the counting-hardness sources for the width-preserving causal reduction.
body.interpretation: For envelopes with \(b\le2\), minimal failure supports can be streamed with certified polynomial delay and exhaustion.  For larger districts, the unconditional algorithm is an exact offline compiler whose runtime should be reported together with the number of raw projected Steiner witnesses and the number rejected by global domination.  Reliability and derivative computation apply after the obstruction hypergraph has been compiled; they do not convert the candidate-sensitive general compiler into a delay algorithm.
body.technical_internal_limitation: For already accepted obstructions \(B_1,\ldots,B_q\), a prospective support \(H\) avoids domination exactly when \(B_i\nsubseteq H\) for every \(i\), equivalently when \(E^{?}\setminus H\) intersects every \(B_i\). Thus partial pruning contains a hypergraph-transversal constraint coupled to existential core choice and multiple-root reachability. Bounded \(b\) does not supply the required extension oracle. The proved general offline procedure does not perform this partial pruning: it exhausts raw minimal directed-Steiner subgraphs and acts only after a full label support \(H\) is available, retaining the designated \(C_c(H)\) witness, applying all-core one-edge-deletion tests, and using least-core ownership. These completed-candidate filters prove exact-once final output and candidate-sensitive total time, but provide no partial-support state, child partition, nonempty-completion test, or accepted-output delay bound. General-\(b\) delay remains exactly Open-Ended Question~\ref{oeq:canonical-partial-support-recursion}.
body.honest_scope: The proved results are the sparse-core reduction; an exact offline general-\(b\) enumeration based on completed-candidate filtering, with total time \(2^{O(b\log(b+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n)(1+W)\); the complete \(b\le2\) labelled-transition-DAG polynomial-delay algorithm; and the width-two counting reduction. Here \(W\) counts raw projected minimal directed-Steiner subgraphs with cores and witnesses separately, so raw label-set repetitions are charged separately. ‘Exact once’ applies only to final emitted obstructions after the completed-support \(C_c(H)\), deletion, and ownership tests; it does not assert duplicate-free raw witnesses or solve partial-support pruning. General-\(b\) accepted-output delay, including a finite partial state, child iterator, and nonempty-completion test, remains Open-Ended Question~\ref{oeq:canonical-partial-support-recursion}. Reliability and derivative evaluation apply only after \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) is explicit, and no implementation or probability-calibration claim is made.
